newsitem.title: CANADA: Newbridge shares recover some lost ground.
newsitem.headline: Newbridge shares recover some lost ground.

text.p: Shares in Newbridge Networks Corp on Wednesday recovered some ground lost since last week on analysts' downgrades and minor estimate reductions.

"It's starting to recover. Basically I think investors are taking a good hard look at the stock -- why it's dropped since last Tuesday and the reasons for the analysts' downgrades," said Robert MacLellan at Dillon Read.
But he said the move did not constitute a complete reversal of recent weakness.
"A dollar in Newbridge isn't a recovery or a drop. It's daily trading," MacLellan added.
Newbridge shares rose 1.90 to 39.50 on the Toronto Stock Exchange in brisk trade. In New York, it added 1-3/4 to 29-5/8.
Newbridge tumbled on Tuesday after Merrill Lynch cut the stock to a near-term neutral from a near-term accumulate. It kept the stock as a long-term accumulate.
That followed other brokerage downgrades last week after the company posted earnings a U.S. cent shy of consensus estimates.
Some analysts expressed concern about Newbridge's ability to deliver a pleasant surprise in its fiscal third quarter.
"It's still an attractive stock," said MacLellan, who said it had dropped to relatively inexpensive levels.
"We continue to maintain our buy recommendation. We see no fundamental reason for investors to step out of the stock."
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
